cards.text: Judah has a new king, Abijah, and he reigns in Jerusalem for three years. He takes the throne in the eighteenth year of Jeroboam's reign over the rest of Israel. And there's war between Abijah and Jeroboam.
Then it's battle time. Abijah marches out with an army of 400,000 chosen men.

cards.question: Jeroboam lines up his own chosen men against Abijah. How does Jeroboam's army compare to Abijah's?

cards.text: DOUBLE, friend! Abijah looks at all that and climbs up on Mount Zemaraim, in the hill country of Ephraim.

cards.question: Abijah is up on Mount Zemaraim with Jeroboam's huge army below. What does he do from up there?

answers.text: He calls out to Jeroboam and all Israel
He sends spies to scout their camp
He offers them gold to buy peace

cards.question: Abijah shouts, "Hear me, O Jeroboam and all Israel!" His first point: what does he say the LORD gave to David and his descendants forever by a covenant of salt?

cards.text: Next, Abijah turns to Jeroboam son of Nebat. Abijah reminds everybody that Jeroboam used to be a servant of Solomon son of David.

cards.question: Abijah says Jeroboam, Solomon's own servant, rose up and rebelled against his master.

cards.text: Abijah says worthless and wicked men gathered around Jeroboam to resist Solomon's son Rehoboam, back when Rehoboam was young, inexperienced and unable to resist them. Friend, that was me my first week in the junk drawer, losing staring contests to the rubber bands I shared it with.

cards.question: Now Abijah talks about the army in front of him. He tells Jeroboam's soldiers they're a small army.
Abijah says they think they can resist the kingdom of the LORD. And he says they have with them the ___ that Jeroboam made for them as gods.
Next, Abijah asks Jeroboam's army about the LORD's priests, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites. What does he say Israel did to them?

cards.text: Then they made their own priests, like the peoples of other lands, and now whoever comes with a young bull and seven rams can become a priest of things that are not gods. A bull and seven rams and you're IN, friend, and that's not a calling, that's a cover charge.

cards.question: Turning to Judah, Abijah says they have not forsaken the LORD.

cards.text: In Judah, Abijah says, the priests who minister to the LORD are sons of Aaron, and the Levites attend to their duties. The real deal, no cover charge.

cards.question: Abijah says that every morning and every evening, Judah's priests present burnt ___ and fragrant ___ to the LORD.

cards.text: They set out the showbread and light the gold lampstand every evening. Then Abijah says, "We are carrying out the requirements of the LORD our God, while you have forsaken Him."

cards.question: Abijah finishes by saying God Himself is with Judah as their head, and His priests with their trumpets sound the battle call. What does he warn the children of Israel not to do?

answers.text: Fight against the LORD the God of their fathers
Come any closer to Mount Zemaraim

cards.text: Big speech from the mountain. But Jeroboam has a move of his own.

cards.question: Jeroboam stays in front of Judah's army. Where does he send some of his troops?

answers.text: Around behind Judah to ambush them
Up the mountain to grab Abijah

cards.text: Judah turns and finds out the battle is both before and behind them. Front AND back, friend, and I'd have turned right back around like I saw NOTHING.

cards.question: Judah's trapped, with battle in front and behind. What do the men of Judah do?
Then the priests blow the trumpets. What do the men of Judah do next?
When the men of Judah raise the cry, ___ routs Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.

cards.text: The Israelites flee before Judah, and God delivers them into their hands. Then Abijah and his people strike them with a mighty blow.

cards.question: Abijah and his people strike Israel with a mighty blow. How many chosen men of Israel fall?

cards.text: So the Israelites are subdued at that time, and the men of Judah prevail. PREVAIL, friend, and I spent years losing to a drawer that wouldn't open from the inside.

cards.question: Why do the men of Judah prevail over Israel?

answers.text: They relied on the LORD the God of their fathers
They had the bigger and stronger army
They struck first and took Israel by surprise

cards.text: Then Abijah chases Jeroboam and captures some cities from him, villages and all.

cards.question: Abijah captures ___ from Jeroboam, along with Jeshanah and Ephron.
After losing those cities, Jeroboam recovers his power while Abijah is still king.

cards.text: Not once in Abijah's days. And the LORD struck Jeroboam down, and he died.

cards.question: After the battle, Abijah grows strong.

cards.text: Abijah marries fourteen wives and becomes the father of twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters. Thirty-eight kids, friend, and I thought SIX cookie cutters kept me busy.
The rest of Abijah's acts, his ways and his words are written in the Treatise of the Prophet Iddo. Now that's one king whose story did NOT end up in the back of a junk drawer.

rule.text: He calls the baker "baker" or "friend," and talks to one baker at a time. Never "my baker," "kids" or "sweetie."

findings.problem: The joke doesn't match the core action. Verse 7 is about a young, inexperienced king who is unable to resist a gang of worthless and wicked men gathered against him. Losing staring contests to rubber bands is a different action, and rubber bands have no eyes, so a stranger would say "huh?". The comparison also casts his drawer friends, who were "all in it together" with him, in the role of the worthless and wicked men.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The joke invents a new drawer pastime: staring contests with the rubber bands. The backstory gives "rubber band stretching contests," not staring contests. It also says that early in the drawer he "didn't talk much" and "didn't joke at all." Jokes may invent small moments around his bakery, not new details of his drawer years.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: "Turning to Judah, Abijah says..." reads as if Abijah starts speaking to Judah. The text shows he is still speaking to Jeroboam and Israel. Verse 10 says "as for us," verse 11 says "while you have forsaken Him," and verse 12 says "O children of Israel." He has only turned to talking about Judah.

rule.text: He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: Two wrong answers are near-matches. "gifts" means nearly the same as "offerings." A baker could argue for "prayers" in place of "incense," since Scripture pairs incense with prayer (Ps 141:2; Rev 5:8).

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank asks the baker to complete the exact wording of the line ("burnt ___ and fragrant ___"). It tests wording they haven't seen, not meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The right answer, "Fight against the LORD the God of their fathers," stands out. It is longer than the wrong answers and is the only one in Bible phrasing ("the God of their fathers"). The wrong answers, "Come any closer to Mount Zemaraim" and "Cross the border into Judah," are short and plain.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The answers aren't the same kind of thing. "God" and "Shishak" are persons, but "Moab" is a nation. Shishak and Moab also appear nowhere in the passage or in earlier cards, which makes the right answer obvious.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The right answer, "They relied on the LORD the God of their fathers," is the only answer in Bible phrasing ("the God of their fathers"), so it stands out from the plain wrong answers.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
